task_2.title: Preserve request headers in urlopen
task_2.description: The 2.2.1 update fixes a regression from 2.2.0 where HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen automatically coerced ordinary request headers into HTTPHeaderDict while merging proxy headers. That coercion exposed HTTPHeaderDict limitations with byte-valued header values and could raise TypeError for header inputs that were previously accepted.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen preserves caller-provided non-proxy request headers without prematurely coercing them into HTTPHeaderDict, so supported header values such as bytes do not fail because of HTTPHeaderDict behavior.

expectation.grounded: HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen should continue to combine request headers with configured proxy_headers when an HTTP tunnel is not required, but it must not automatically cast the non-proxy headers argument to HTTPHeaderDict as part of that merge. Header mappings containing byte values should not fail solely because HTTPHeaderDict cannot currently represent or merge those values correctly.
expectation.conceptual: Requests should keep accepting header inputs that worked before 2.2.0. Adding proxy headers must not change ordinary request headers into a stricter representation that rejects otherwise usable values.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public urlopen API, the proxy_headers merge semantics, or the HTTP tunnel behavior. The outgoing headers should still be copied before mutation so the caller's header object is not modified in place.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be limited to avoiding the regression while preserving existing proxy behavior and caller data isolation.

behavior: When HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen handles a request path where an HTTP tunnel is not required, non-proxy request headers are copied rather than converted to HTTPHeaderDict.
Configured proxy headers are still merged into the copied outgoing headers for non-tunnel proxy requests.
Caller-provided header mappings with byte-valued entries no longer trigger failures caused by HTTPHeaderDict coercion during urlopen processing.
The original headers object supplied by the caller remains unmodified when proxy headers are added.
acceptance_criteria: Given a call to HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen with non-proxy request headers containing byte values, when the request is processed on a path that does not require an HTTP tunnel, then it should not fail due to HTTPHeaderDict conversion.

Given configured proxy_headers and caller-supplied request headers, when HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen processes a non-tunnel proxy request, then the outgoing headers should include the proxy headers while preserving the caller's header values.
Given a mutable header mapping passed by the caller, when HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen merges proxy headers, then the caller's original mapping should not be mutated.
Given a request path where an HTTP tunnel is required, when HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen handles headers, then the existing tunnel-specific header behavior should remain unchanged.

task_1.title: Correct Emscripten HTTPS verification warnings
task_1.description: The update fixes urllib3's Emscripten transport so HTTPS requests are treated as verified under browser-managed TLS validation, preventing spurious InsecureRequestWarning emissions while preserving unverified behavior for plain HTTP.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 running on Emscripten does not warn that HTTPS requests are insecure when those requests are validated by the browser-managed TLS layer.

expectation.grounded: EmscriptenHTTPConnection should report an unverified connection state, while EmscriptenHTTPSConnection should report a verified connection state. As a result, urllib3.exceptions.InsecureRequestWarning should not be emitted for Emscripten HTTPS requests solely because Python TLS verification is not used, and HTTP requests should remain treated as unverified.
expectation.conceptual: Secure browser-backed HTTPS requests should not be surfaced to users as insecure, while non-secure HTTP requests should continue to be recognized as unverified.

constraints.grounded: The change must be limited to the Emscripten connection verification semantics and must not weaken HTTPS handling, disable browser TLS verification assumptions, or suppress InsecureRequestWarning for genuinely unverified HTTP connections.
constraints.conceptual: Do not hide real insecure-connection warnings or change behavior for unrelated runtimes; only correct the false warning for browser-backed HTTPS.

behavior: Emscripten HTTP connections expose an unverified state.
Emscripten HTTPS connections expose a verified state because verification is handled by the browser environment.
HTTPS requests made through urllib3's Emscripten support no longer trigger InsecureRequestWarning solely due to the absence of Python-controlled TLS verification.
Plain HTTP requests through urllib3's Emscripten support remain classified as unverified and can still produce the appropriate insecure-request warning behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When an HTTPS request is made through urllib3 in an Emscripten environment, it should complete without emitting urllib3.exceptions.InsecureRequestWarning solely because TLS verification is delegated to browser APIs.
When an HTTP request is made through urllib3 in an Emscripten environment, it should continue to be represented as unverified and retain the existing insecure-request warning behavior.
When connection verification state is inspected for Emscripten transports, HTTP and HTTPS connections should expose different verification states that match their security semantics.
When urllib3 is used outside the Emscripten transport path, connection warning behavior should remain unchanged.

task_3.title: Clarify truncated chunked response errors
task_3.description: Chunked response parsing now distinguishes a response that ends before the next chunk length is received from a response that sends an invalid chunk length. Premature termination at a chunk boundary is surfaced as a protocol-level error instead of an invalid chunk-length error, while malformed non-empty chunk length data keeps the existing behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that chunked HTTP responses which terminate before sending the next chunk length are reported as premature protocol termination rather than as malformed chunk-length data.

expectation.grounded: When urllib3.response.HTTPResponse is reading a chunked response and the stream ends at the point where the next chunk-size line should be received, consuming chunks through the response API should raise urllib3.exceptions.ProtocolError. If a non-empty chunk-size line is present but cannot be parsed as a valid hexadecimal chunk length, it should continue to raise urllib3.exceptions.InvalidChunkLength.
expectation.conceptual: A truncated chunked response should be classified as an incomplete protocol exchange, while an actually malformed chunk-size value should remain classified as invalid chunk metadata.

constraints.grounded: Do not change successful chunk parsing, chunk extension handling, or the existing InvalidChunkLength behavior for non-empty invalid chunk-size data. The premature-termination path should still close the affected HTTPResponse before surfacing the error.
constraints.conceptual: Only the error classification for an absent chunk length at end of stream should change; valid responses and genuinely malformed chunk headers should behave as before.

behavior: A chunked response that reaches end of stream before any next chunk-size data is received is treated as premature response termination.
That premature-termination condition raises ProtocolError instead of InvalidChunkLength.
The affected HTTPResponse is closed before the premature-termination error is exposed to the caller.
A non-empty but invalid chunk-size value still raises InvalidChunkLength.
Valid chunk-size values continue to be parsed normally and do not change response iteration behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a chunked response stream that ends exactly where the next chunk length should begin, when a caller consumes the response chunks, it should raise ProtocolError rather than InvalidChunkLength.
Given a chunked response stream that sends non-empty invalid chunk-length data, when a caller consumes the response chunks, it should still raise InvalidChunkLength.
Given a valid chunked response stream, when a caller consumes the response chunks, it should continue to yield the response body chunks normally.
When the premature end-of-stream condition is detected while reading the next chunk length, the response should be closed before the error is surfaced.

task_4.title: Clarify ProtocolError for unexpected response bodies
task_4.description: urllib3 2.2.1 improves the error reported when a response that should not contain content still sends body bytes. Instead of surfacing a misleading incomplete-read or broken-connection diagnostic, the raised ProtocolError now identifies the unexpected content condition while preserving the existing exception type and underlying cause.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that HTTP responses expected to be empty but received with body content fail with a clear ProtocolError explaining that content is not allowed, instead of presenting the condition as a generic incomplete read or broken connection.

expectation.grounded: When urllib3 response reading or streaming encounters an IncompleteRead whose known expected byte count is the negative of the known partial byte count, it should raise urllib3.exceptions.ProtocolError with diagnostics indicating that the response is not permitted to contain content. The original IncompleteRead should remain available as the underlying error. Other IncompleteRead cases should continue to be reported through ProtocolError using the existing broken-connection semantics.
expectation.conceptual: Consumers should get a clear protocol-level error when a server or mock sends a body for a response that must be empty. The error should make the unexpected-content problem apparent without changing the public exception category callers already handle.

constraints.grounded: Do not change successful response reading behavior, timeout handling, content decoding, or the ProtocolError exception type. Do not apply the new unexpected-content diagnostic to ordinary incomplete reads unless the IncompleteRead values indicate that all observed bytes are excess content.
constraints.conceptual: This is a diagnostic fix only: valid responses should behave as before, and unrelated connection failures should keep their previous meaning.

behavior: IncompleteRead failures with known partial and expected byte counts where the expected count exactly offsets the partial bytes are classified as excess content on a response that may not have a body.
That classified condition is wrapped in ProtocolError with user-facing diagnostics about disallowed response content rather than generic broken-connection wording.
The original IncompleteRead remains associated with the ProtocolError for callers that inspect the underlying cause or arguments.
IncompleteRead failures that do not match the excess-content condition continue to be wrapped as broken-connection ProtocolError failures.
HTTPException and OSError failures during response reading retain their existing ProtocolError wrapping behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a response that is expected to have no body, when body bytes are received and response content is read, it should raise ProtocolError whose diagnostic clearly identifies unexpected or disallowed response content.
When a caller consumes such a response through normal read or stream paths, it should still observe ProtocolError rather than a new public exception type.
When the underlying incomplete-read condition represents missing data rather than excess disallowed content, it should continue to be reported as a broken connection.
When response reading fails for timeout, HTTP-layer, or OS-layer reasons unrelated to excess content, existing exception behavior should be preserved.
When a valid response is read successfully, response data handling should be unchanged.
